Apple is expected to launch the iPhone 18 series this September as usual, but this year's new device release may echo the unusual circumstances of the iPhone launch during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

How this fall's iPhone launch event may differ from Apple's past launch patterns

Apple has many highly successful products, but the iPhone has always been its flagship, accounting for a large share of the company's total revenue.

Therefore, it's understandable that Apple is committed to maintaining consistency in iPhone launches. By sticking to a predictable new iPhone release schedule, the company can better please Wall Street and consumers.

Generally speaking, Apple unveils new iPhones in early September—typically introducing four new models—and all go on sale in late September.

But 2020 became an exception due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

The fall 2020 iPhone lineup was not announced until October, with only two new models initially going on sale, while the other two were delayed until November.

This year, rumors suggest Apple's launch plans may once again see similar disruptions.

Although a September launch event is still expected, Apple may not put all new iPhone models on sale at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models are likely to launch initially: the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The highly anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra is expected to make its debut in September, but rumors suggest its release date may be pushed back slightly, potentially going on sale several weeks after the Pro models.

Apple may also deviate from its usual approach in terms of the total number of new iPhone models.

If rumors of the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 being delayed until spring 2027 are true, only three new models will debut this fall—the smallest fall iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether due to strategic considerations, challenges posed by the global memory crisis, or the difficulty of mass-producing an entirely new foldable device, Apple's fall 2026 may repeat many of the scenarios from 2020.

What new iPhones would you like to see Apple release this fall? Let us know in the comments.
